newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz industrial business down, but sees growth.
newsitem.headline: Allianz industrial business down, but sees growth.

text.p: Allianz AG Holding said on Tuesday its industrial insurance business had declined since the start of 1995 but the giant insurer said it still hoped to expand its leading role in the sector.

Reiner Hagemann, management board chairman of domestic non-life unit Allianz Versicherungs AG, told a news conference that the company had suffered a two percent drop in industrial insurance premiums to 2.3 billion marks ($1.5 billion) in 1995 and that the downward trend had continued this year.

In Germany, where Allianz has a 25 percent market share in industrial insurance, structural crises in an industry plagued by weak demand and Allianz's own risk-oriented underwriting policy contributed to the decline, Hagemann said.
Allianz, Europe's leading insurer, would enhance its position in industrial insurance by improving efficiency, customer acceptance and earnings power, Hagemann said.
Claims were high in industrial insurance, Hagemann said, so that cost management might take on added importance in future.
Hagemann also urged better risk control within companies themselves. In fire insurance Allianz had paid 500 million marks for 316 major fires causing dmaages of one million marks or more in 1995.

As well as expanding into German credit insurance via its acquisition of Hermes Kreditversicherungs AG, the group planned to strengthen its industrial business in eastern Europe and planned to achieve premium income there of around 600 million marks in 1996.
